target_customer: Patients with Crohn's disease and other chronic inflammatory conditions, reached through pharma development and licensing; today the paying parties are grant funders and investors
problem: Current treatments for inflammatory bowel disease suppress the immune system. The company aims to restore intestinal innate immune function and wound healing instead.
business_model: Preclinical drug development, with value realized through partnering, licensing or acquisition
product_category: Therapeutics, bacterial derived small molecules for inflammatory disease

founders.name: Katerina Chatzi
founders.background_notes: YC page says she was a postdoc at Harvard; company site adds immunology, biochemistry and bacteriology background and a KU Leuven postdoc.

founders.name: Jasper Edgar Neggers
prior_employers: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
education: KU Leuven, BSc, MSc and PhD in Biomedical Sciences
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page; also described there as inventing a CRISPR directed evolution technology for drug target deconvolution.

investors: Propel a Cure for Crohn's disease

competitors.name: Vedanta Biosciences (VE202 with Janssen)
competitors.what: Defined multistrain live bacterial consortium for Crohn's disease
competitors.traction_then: Clinical stage candidate in a Janssen collaboration per a 2020 industry listing

competitors.name: Finch Therapeutics (FIN-525 with Takeda)
competitors.traction_then: Early stage candidate per a 2020 industry listing

technical_complexity.rationale: Discovering and validating bacterial derived molecules that modulate innate immunity requires research grade biology, animal models and years of preclinical and clinical work.

defensibility.rationale: Patentable molecules and scientific know how could be protective, but no issued patents were checked and the microbiome field had many well funded entrants.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Pharma funded microbiome programs existed, and the sector sentiment dropped after Seres' trial setback per one source. No incumbent has acquired or copied Promakhos as far as found.

market_need_then: The company's own materials cite over 500,000 US Crohn's patients and about 10B USD annual cost. Existing immunosuppressants leave many patients without durable control.

branding.domain_note: Uses promakhos.com; no purchase history found.

identity.logo: not described by an opened source
identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific and mission led; tagline says creating transformative medicines for people with inflammatory diseases.

brand_strength.rationale: A science driven biotech brand with a distinctive name but no press about the brand or community. Recognition comes from grants and conference appearances.

outcome_analysis: Promakhos remains active with a team of 1 to 10 and has financed itself mostly through non dilutive grants since 2021, including an NIH SBIR and Crohn's patient foundation awards. No equity round above a small seed was verified, and no clinical data or partnership has been reported. The model needs far more capital than grants provide, so progress depends on raising a real seed or partnering.
notes: Seed size is unverified: several aggregators list about 125K USD (extruct dates it 2021-08-26) and Dealroom lists a 2.3M seed entry, so no equity round is recorded. Caplight totals 594K USD which matches the grants. The Propel a Cure date appears as 2024-02 on the company site and LinkedIn snippet but 2025 in another aggregator. The grant rows use the company website as source. The competitor entries come from a search result that listed Vedanta and Finch candidates; the specific Nature article was not opened, so the attribution is unverified. Name origin is not stated by the company; the Greek word promachos means front line fighter but the company's intent is unconfirmed.
